questions.question: What are the three tiers of software reconciliation results in Software Asset Management?

options.text: Product Results, License Results, Installation Results
Product Results, Software Model Results, License Metric Results
Publisher Results, Model Results, Entitlement Results
Discovery Results, Normalization Results, Compliance Results

explanation.correct: Software reconciliation generates three tiers of results: Product Results (for all models and installations associated with a software product), Software Model Results (for each individual software model), and License Metric Results (for each license metric associated with the software model).

wrongAnswers.explanation: Installation Results is not a separate tier; installations are tracked within Product Results and Software Model Results.
These are not the official tier names in SAM reconciliation.
Discovery and Normalization are separate processes from reconciliation results.

source.excerpt: There are three tiers of reconciliation results: Product Results, Software Model Results, License Metric Results

questions.question: Which related lists appear on Product Results records after software reconciliation? (Choose three.)

explanation.correct: Product Results records include related lists for: Software Model Results, Licensed Installs, Unlicensed Installs, and Removal Candidates. For SAP, Unlicensed Users appears instead of Unlicensed Installs.

wrongAnswers.explanation: Discovery Models are separate entities from reconciliation results; they are created during discovery, not as related lists on Product Results.
Transform Maps are used for data imports, not as related lists on reconciliation results.

source.excerpt: The following related lists appear when you select a Product Results record: Software Model Results, Licensed Installs, Unlicensed Installs, Removal Candidates

questions.question: How often does software reconciliation run by default in Software Asset Management?

explanation.correct: Reconciliation runs weekly or on demand for a specific publisher or all publishers. When reconciliation runs, it calculates compliance based on how many rights are in use compared to the number of active rights purchased.

wrongAnswers.explanation: The default schedule is weekly, not daily, though reconciliation can be triggered on demand.
Reconciliation runs more frequently than monthly - it runs weekly by default.
Reconciliation is not triggered automatically by discovery scans; it has its own weekly schedule.

source.excerpt: Reconciliation runs weekly or on demand for a specific publisher or all publishers.

questions.question: Which API version should be used for new IBM License Metric Tool (ILMT) or BigFix Inventory integrations?

explanation.correct: Version 1 of the ILMT and BigFix Inventory integration APIs have been deprecated by IBM. For new integrations, version 2 of the APIs should be used. The Software Asset Management application continues to support existing v1 integrations.

wrongAnswers.explanation: While v1 APIs are still supported for existing integrations, they are deprecated and should not be used for new integrations.
There is no v3 API mentioned; v2 is the current recommended version.
The REST Table API is a general ServiceNow API, not specifically for ILMT/BigFix integration.

source.excerpt: Version 1 of the ILMT and BigFix Inventory integration APIs have been deprecated by IBM. If you are setting up an ILMT or BigFix Inventory integration for the first time, use version 2 of the APIs instead.

questions.question:
Which of the following statements about IBM ILMT integration prerequisites are true?
a) ILMT version 9.2.7 or later must be installed.
b) IBM ILMT agents must be configured to comply with IBM usage measurement guidelines.
c) The Software Asset Management Professional for IBM plugin must be activated.
d) ILMT can only be installed on physical hosts, not virtual machines.

explanation.correct: Statements a, b, and c are true. Statement d is false because ILMT can be installed on both physical hosts AND virtual machines (VMs).

wrongAnswers.explanation: Statement d is false - ILMT can be installed on a physical host or virtual machine.
Statement a is true - ILMT version 9.2.7 or later is required.
Statement c is also true - the IBM plugin must be activated to get the IBM Server connection alias.

source.excerpt: Install, set up, and run ILMT or BigFix Inventory on a physical host or virtual machine (VM). Install ILMT version 9.2.7 or later. Configure your IBM ILMT agents to scan your physical hosts or VMs in compliance with IBM usage measurement guidelines.

questions.question: An organization uses Visual Studio subscriptions. When reconciliation runs, Microsoft software installed on production environments appears as unlicensed. What should be configured to ensure proper license coverage?

options.text: Add product install conditions to Visual Studio software models limiting installations to development or test environments
Increase the inference percent to 100% on Visual Studio software models
Disable environment validation in SAM properties
Create separate entitlements for each environment type

explanation.correct: Visual Studio subscriptions only cover development or test environments. Product install conditions should be added to Visual Studio software models to define where software can be installed. For example, conditions like 'Installed on contains dev' or 'Installed on contains test'. Production installations require separate Microsoft licenses.

wrongAnswers.explanation: Inference percent relates to suite component detection, not environment validation.
There is no such property to disable environment validation; this would violate Microsoft licensing terms.
Visual Studio subscriptions specifically cover only dev/test environments by Microsoft licensing terms; separate entitlements won't change this.

source.excerpt: Add product install conditions to your Visual Studio software models that apply across all software models including downgrades and editions. Install conditions define where the software can be installed. For Visual Studio, installing the software anywhere that is not a development or test environment is a violation of the Microsoft license agreement.

questions.question: What data is retrieved by the ILMT and BigFix Inventory integration? (Choose two.)

options.text: Products, components, editions, hosts, and virtual machines
License usage based on product use
License usage based on component use

explanation.correct: The ILMT/BigFix integration retrieves historical software installation data including products, components, editions, hosts, virtual machines, and license usage. Note that license usage is based on product use, not component use.

wrongAnswers.explanation: License usage is based on product use, NOT component use. This is explicitly stated in the documentation.
User credentials are not retrieved by this integration; it focuses on software installation and licensing data.

source.excerpt: The Software Asset Management application retrieves historical software installation data within the aggregated period that you defined in ILMT or BigFix Inventory. This data includes products, components, editions, hosts, virtual machines, and license usage. Note: License usage is based on product use and not component use.

questions.question: Where can you access the navigation path to view reconciliation results in the Software Asset Workspace?

options.text: Software Asset Workspace > Reconciliation > Historical Results
Software Asset Workspace > License usage (then select a publisher card)

explanation.correct: In the Software Asset Workspace, navigate to Software Asset Workspace > License usage, then select a publisher card and select a Product Results record to view product result details. In Core UI, the path is All > Software Asset > Reconciliation > Historical Results.

wrongAnswers.explanation: This is the Core UI navigation path, not the Software Asset Workspace path.
Discovery results are separate from reconciliation results.
There is no 'Compliance > Reports' path for reconciliation results; use 'License usage'.

source.excerpt: Software Asset Workspace: Navigate to Software Asset Workspace > License usage. Select a publisher card and then select a Product Results record to view the product result details.

questions.question: What is the default frequency for the software reconciliation scheduled job?

explanation.correct: Reconciliation is a scheduled job that runs at a specified frequency, with the default being weekly. It can also be run on demand for specific or all publishers, groups, and subgroups.

wrongAnswers.explanation: Daily is not the default; weekly is the default frequency.
Monthly would be too infrequent for accurate compliance tracking.
Reconciliation has a scheduled job by default (weekly), though it can also be run on demand.

source.excerpt: Reconciliation is a scheduled job that is run at a specified frequency (default is weekly). It can also be run on demand for specific or all publishers, groups, and subgroups.

questions.question: Which grouping values can be used for software reconciliation? (Choose three.)

explanation.correct: Group and subgroup values for reconciliation include country, department, company, region, or cost center. These properties can be set in Software Asset > Administration > Properties.

wrongAnswers.explanation: Hardware model is not a valid reconciliation grouping value.
Network segment is not used for software reconciliation grouping.

source.excerpt: Group and subgroup values include country, department, company, region, or cost center. Default group and subgroup properties can be set in Software Asset > Administration > Properties.

questions.question: Which license type requires linkage to a base perpetual license for SAM to reconcile it properly?

explanation.correct: Software Assurance (Microsoft) and Maintenance (non-Microsoft) entitlements must be linked to a base perpetual license to activate the entitlements. SAM does not reconcile these entitlements unless they are related to base perpetual licenses.

wrongAnswers.explanation: Subscription licenses work independently based on subscription portal data.
Perpetual licenses are standalone and do not require linking to other licenses.
Upgrade licenses allow edition upgrades but do not specifically require perpetual license linkage for reconciliation.

source.excerpt: Software Assurance: Must be linked to a base perpetual license to activate the entitlements. Software Asset Management does not reconcile software assurance entitlements unless they are linked to base perpetual licenses.

questions.question: An organization has a Perpetual + Software Assurance license for Microsoft SQL Server. What benefit is automatically applied by SAM during reconciliation?

options.text: Software Assurance benefits including unlimited virtualization for Datacenter editions
Automatic software uninstallation on non-compliant devices

explanation.correct: Software Asset Management automatically applies Software Assurance benefits for Perpetual + Software Assurance licenses. Benefits include new version rights, license mobility, and unlimited virtualization for products like Windows Server Datacenter Edition.

wrongAnswers.explanation: SAM does not generate license keys; keys come from the software publisher.
Technical support comes from Microsoft, not ServiceNow.
Automatic uninstallation requires configuring reclamation rules and Client Software Distribution.

source.excerpt: Perpetual + Software Assurance: Software Asset Management automatically applies the Software Assurance benefits. Benefits include unlimited virtualization: License the physical host for products such as Windows Server Datacenter Edition.

questions.question: What role is required to view software reconciliation results in SAM?

explanation.correct: Users with the sam_user role can view reconciliation results. This role provides read access to SAM data including compliance status and license positions.

wrongAnswers.explanation: sam_admin has additional administrative capabilities but sam_user is sufficient for viewing results.
sam_developer is for creating custom metrics and scripts, not required for viewing results.
The ITIL role is for IT Service Management, not specifically for SAM reconciliation access.

source.excerpt: Users with the sam_user role can view reconciliation results.

questions.question: Which navigation path accesses software reconciliation results in the Core UI?

options.text: All > Software Asset > Reconciliation > Historical Results

explanation.correct: In Core UI, navigate to All > Software Asset > Reconciliation > Historical Results to view reconciliation results. Select a reconciliation result, then select a Product Results record to view details.

wrongAnswers.explanation: Reports is a different module; reconciliation results are under the Reconciliation menu.
CMDB does not contain the reconciliation results; they are in Software Asset.
There is no License Management top-level module; use Software Asset.

source.excerpt: Core UI: Navigate to All > Software Asset > Reconciliation > Historical Results. Select a reconciliation result. On the Reconciliation Result form, select a Product Results record.

questions.question: Which license metric group requires the SaaS License Management plugin to be installed?

explanation.correct: Installing SaaS License Management adds the Subscription and Consumption metric groups. The Subscription group includes User Subscription, and the Consumption group includes SaaS Consumption metrics.

wrongAnswers.explanation: Common metric group is available in the base SAM application without additional plugins.
Concurrent Licenses require the Software Asset Management Professional for Engineering Applications plugin, not SaaS License Management.
Adobe metrics require the Adobe publisher pack, not the SaaS License Management plugin.

questions.question: What is the difference between Floating and Token license metrics in the Concurrent Licenses group?

options.text: Floating shares software licenses; Token shares a pool of tokens that may require multiple tokens per software checkout
Floating is for cloud software; Token is for on-premise software
Floating allows unlimited users; Token has a strict user limit
There is no difference; they are aliases for the same metric

explanation.correct: Floating licenses share and manage a pool of software licenses, checking out one license per request. Token licenses share a pool of tokens, and each software access may check out one or more tokens. Both are based on peak usage.

wrongAnswers.explanation: Both Floating and Token are concurrent license types that can apply to any deployment model.
Both are limited by the pool size; neither allows unlimited users.
They are distinct metrics with different licensing units (software licenses vs. tokens).

questions.question: An organization uses Oracle databases on VMware. Which property controls the level of aggregation for Oracle license reconciliation?

explanation.correct: The com.snc.samp.oracle.reconlevel property sets the aggregation level for Oracle Database and WebLogic Server licenses on VMware. Options are ESX, ESX cluster (default), or vCenter(s).

wrongAnswers.explanation: This property sets general reconciliation grouping (Company, Region, etc.), not Oracle-specific aggregation.
This property enables host affinity rules for Oracle at the vCenter(s) level, but doesn't set the aggregation level.
This property controls parallel scheduled jobs for reconciliation, not Oracle aggregation.

questions.question: What are the three aggregation levels available for Oracle reconciliation on VMware?

explanation.correct: The three aggregation levels are: ESX (considers all processor cores on the ESX host), ESX cluster (considers all processors on every ESX server within a cluster — default), and vCenter(s) (considers all processor cores on every ESX server).

wrongAnswers.explanation: These are generic virtualization terms, not the specific SAM property values.
Physical/Virtual/Hybrid are deployment models, not Oracle reconciliation aggregation levels.
Server/Datacenter/Enterprise are Microsoft licensing tiers, not Oracle aggregation levels.

questions.question: How does the Microsoft Per Core (with CAL) license metric handle VMware clusters with vMotion or DRS enabled?

options.text: Only the ESX server currently hosting the VM is licensed
The peak capacity of cores on all ESX servers within the cluster is considered for licensing
Only the ESX server with the most cores is licensed
Each VM is licensed individually regardless of the host

explanation.correct: When vMotion or DRS is enabled, any VM can move to any ESX Server within the cluster. Therefore, the peak capacity of cores on ALL ESX Servers in the cluster is considered for the rights needed to license the cluster.

wrongAnswers.explanation: With vMotion/DRS, VMs can move between hosts, so licensing a single host is insufficient.
All ESX servers in the cluster are considered, not just the one with the most cores.
Per Core (with CAL) licenses at the cluster level for ESX servers, not per individual VM.

questions.question: IBM Processor Value Unit (PVU) licensing supports two capacity modes. What are they?

explanation.correct: IBM PVU licensing supports Full capacity (requires licenses for all activated processor cores in the physical hardware environment) and Subcapacity (requires licenses for less than the full capacity of your server or group of servers).

wrongAnswers.explanation: Standard and Enterprise are edition names, not PVU capacity modes.
Per-socket and Per-core are different license metrics, not modes within PVU.
Physical and Virtual describe deployment types; PVU has Full capacity and Subcapacity modes.

questions.question: A customer wants to determine whether to use RHEL Server or RHEL for Virtual Datacenters licenses. Which property controls the optimization threshold?

options.text: The Red Hat Enterprise Linux Server for Virtual Datacenters license cost optimization threshold property

explanation.correct: This property determines whether to use RHEL Server or RHEL for Virtual Datacenters licenses. The default threshold is 3.2, based on the ratio of RHEL Server subscription list price to RHEL for Virtual Datacenters subscription price. It requires the IBM publisher pack.

wrongAnswers.explanation: This property controls Oracle reconciliation aggregation level, not Red Hat licensing.
This property controls Windows Server Datacenter vs Standard Edition licensing optimization, not Red Hat.
This property controls reconciliation grouping, not Red Hat license optimization.

questions.question: How many cores per processor does VMware's Per Processor license metric require by default?

explanation.correct: VMware's Per Processor license metric requires one license per 32 cores per CPU. A 'Maximum cores per processor' metric attribute with a default value of 32 is automatically created on software models for VMware per processor entitlements.

wrongAnswers.explanation: The default is 32 cores per processor, not 16.
The default is 32 cores per processor, not 48.
The default is 32 cores per processor, not 64.
